cases.name: flow-for-a-process
cases.question: Walk me through what happens, step by step, when I type a web address and press Enter.
cases.good:
The browser finds the server, asks for the page and draws it.
```flow
{"title": "From address to page", "steps": ["DNS turns the name into an address", "The browser opens a connection (TCP, then TLS)", "It sends an HTTP request", "The server answers with HTML", "The browser draws the page"]}
```
cases.bad: The browser looks up the name, connects, sends a request and draws the answer.

cases.name: compare-two-options
cases.question: PostgreSQL or SQLite for a small new web app: how do they compare?
cases.good:
Both work; SQLite is simpler, PostgreSQL grows further.
```compare
{"items": [{"title": "SQLite", "points": ["One file, no server", "Great for one machine"]}, {"title": "PostgreSQL", "points": ["A server of its own", "Many writers at once"]}]}
```
cases.bad:
Both work; SQLite is simpler, PostgreSQL grows further.
```compare
{"items": [{"title": "SQLite", "points": ["One file"]}]}
```

cases.name: timeline-for-versions
cases.question: How did HTTP change over the years, version by version?
cases.good:
Each version made the web faster.
```timeline
{"title": "HTTP versions", "events": [{"when": "1991", "what": "HTTP/0.9: one line, HTML only"}, {"when": "1996", "what": "HTTP/1.0: headers"}, {"when": "1997", "what": "HTTP/1.1: kept connections"}, {"when": "2015", "what": "HTTP/2: many requests on one connection"}, {"when": "2022", "what": "HTTP/3: over QUIC"}]}
```
cases.bad:
Each version made the web faster.
```flow
{"steps": ["HTTP/1.0", "HTTP/1.1", "HTTP/2", "HTTP/3"]}
```

cases.name: chart-for-numbers

cases.name: check-when-teaching
cases.question: Teach me what a hash map is, then test me with one question.
cases.good:
A hash map stores values under keys and finds them in one step on average.
```check
{"q": "Why is a lookup in a hash map fast?", "a": "The key's hash points straight at where the value is kept."}
```
cases.bad:
A hash map stores values under keys.

**Question:** Why is a lookup fast?

cases.name: warn-callout
cases.question: Is it fine to build a shell command by pasting what a user typed into it?
cases.good:
No: it lets the user run any command.
```callout
{"tone": "warn", "title": "Shell injection", "text": "Pass the input as an argument, never inside the command's text."}
```
cases.bad:
No: it lets the user run any command.
```callout
{"tone": "tip", "text": "Pass the input as an argument."}
```

cases.name: none-for-a-definition
cases.question: What does idempotent mean, in one sentence?
cases.good: An idempotent action gives the same result however many times you do it, like pressing a lift's call button twice.
cases.bad:
It gives the same result every time.
```flow
{"steps": ["Call once", "Call again", "Same result"]}
```
